# RIndex – Copilot Instructions

RIndex is a modern frontend-only cybersecurity analysis platform built with React, Vite, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS.

Github: https://github.com/homophobiaa/Rindex

The project evaluates user cybersecurity habits such as:
- password strength
- phishing awareness
- account protection
- device security
- privacy exposure
- recovery security

The app uses concepts from:
- Cryptography
- Discrete Mathematics
- Theory of Automata
- Number Systems

The platform MUST remain fully frontend-only.
No backend should ever be introduced unless explicitly requested.

---

# Extremely Important Project Philosophy

RIndex is NOT:
- a fake hacker simulator
- a cringe terminal-style cyberpunk app
- a malware-looking UI
- a generic boring form website

RIndex IS:
- premium
- modern
- trustworthy
- fluid
- highly visual
- privacy-first
- mathematically grounded
- educational
- interactive

The app should feel closer to:
- Linear
- Obsidian
- modern SaaS dashboards
- premium analytics platforms

NOT old-school "hacker movie" aesthetics.

Avoid:
- matrix rain
- green monospace spam
- fake console effects
- over-the-top cyberpunk visuals
- visual clutter

---

# Frontend-Only Privacy Requirement

This project is intentionally frontend-only for privacy and security reasons.

Sensitive calculations MUST happen entirely in the browser.

Important:
- NEVER send passwords or sensitive answers anywhere
- NEVER introduce backend APIs for analysis
- NEVER store passwords
- NEVER log password inputs
- NEVER use localStorage for sensitive data
- NEVER introduce analytics tracking tied to sensitive fields

The app should constantly communicate:
- local browser processing
- transparency
- trust
- open-source visibility

Users should feel safe using the app.

---

# Password Analysis Rules

Users may optionally:
1. Analyze a real password locally
2. Use a safe password-pattern builder

The app MUST clearly explain:
- all calculations happen locally
- no password is transmitted
- no password is stored

The password analysis system should:
- estimate entropy
- estimate brute-force complexity
- detect weak patterns
- detect reused-pattern risk
- visualize strength dynamically

Do not implement fake or misleading "AI security analysis".

---

# Core UX Direction

This app should feel:
- smooth
- animated
- responsive
- interactive
- attention-holding

The experience should avoid:
- long static forms
- large walls of text
- boring layouts
- abrupt transitions

Use:
- progressive disclosure
- animated transitions
- staggered reveals
- interactive cards
- dynamic visual feedback
- visual hierarchy
- polished loading states

Every major interaction should feel intentional.

---

# Animation Philosophy

Framer Motion is a core part of the experience.

Animations should:
- improve flow
- improve readability
- guide attention
- increase perceived quality

Animations should NOT:
- feel excessive
- become distracting
- reduce readability
- hurt performance

Prioritize:
- smoothness
- subtlety
- premium feel

---

# Visualization Requirements

React Flow should be used for:
- attack path visualization
- interconnected risk graphs
- node-based security relationships

Recharts should be used for:
- risk scoring
- category breakdowns
- visual analytics
- animated statistics

Visualizations should be:
- interactive
- clean
- understandable
- visually impressive
- easy to explain during project defense

# Code Quality Rules

- maintainability
- clean structure
- reusable components

Avoid:

- Vite
- TypeScript

# Component Philosophy

Components should be:

Prefer small focused components over massive monolithic files.

---

# Performance Expectations

The app should feel fast and responsive.

Avoid:
- unnecessary rerenders
- heavy animations everywhere
- bloated dependencies
- poor mobile performance

Animations should remain smooth on mid-range hardware.

---

# Accessibility

Maintain reasonable accessibility:
- keyboard navigation where practical
- readable contrast
- clear focus states
- semantic structure

Do not sacrifice usability purely for aesthetics.

---

# Final Goal

The final product should feel like:
- a real startup product
- a premium cybersecurity platform
- an interactive educational tool

The app should immediately impress users visually while also remaining technically believable and mathematically grounded.
